gaps.sentence: ___ sun sets much later in summer.
gaps.explanation: 'The sun' — there is only one, so the definite article is used.

gaps.sentence: ___ poverty remains a serious problem in many large cities.
gaps.explanation: Uncountable abstract nouns in a general sense take no article.
'MA' is pronounced /em/, starting with a vowel sound, so 'an MA'.

gaps.sentence: This is ___ second time you've been late this week.
___ information you sent was extremely helpful.
gaps.explanation: 'The information you sent' — the clause defines it; information is uncountable.

gaps.sentence: The charity provides ___ shelter for homeless families in winter.
gaps.explanation: 'Shelter' is uncountable and general here, so no article is used.

gaps.sentence: She got ___ injury during the warm-up.
gaps.explanation: 'An injury' — vowel sound; 'during the warm-up' is the specific one.

gaps.sentence: He left ___ school at sixteen and went straight into a job.
gaps.explanation: Leave school (finish education) takes no article.
